citation: Lyden et al. (2024). PyPSA-GB: An open-source model of Great Britain’s power system for simulating future energy scenarios. Energy Strategy Reviews 53, 101375.
description: PyPSA-GB is Andrew Lyden and collaborators' electricity-system model with national coverage of Great Britain, built on PyPSA. It supplies detailed transmission, reduced-network and zonal representations for historical analysis and future scenarios, with automated routing to generation, demand and network sources. Users configure study years and scenarios in YAML and run a Snakemake workflow; outputs are constructed networks and power-system optimisation results. The reviewed documentation describes more than 2,000 buses in the detailed representation, 32 in the reduced model and 17 zones. Source is free under MIT; the licence separately states CC-BY-4.0 for ESPENI and ERA5 inputs. A limitation is that historical and projected inputs follow different sources and assumptions, with the reviewed workflow separating years through 2024 from later scenarios. Future upgrades are planning assumptions. PyPSA-GB can assess capacity, dispatch and electrification pathways, specialising PyPSA (model-pypsa) for Great Britain. The README cites the 2024 Energy Strategy Reviews paper. No network files or energy datasets were downloaded.
